name: Level 02
_comment: The hand-authored single-floor registry. It is no longer the composition the viewer loads — rooms/manifest.json points at building.json, and levels are expanded from a unit type by src/types.js — but it is still a valid composition and the fallback path in app.js still reads it. Placements remain unresolved: no accepted anchor fixes where these rooms sit relative to one another. The layout below is a working arrangement chosen so the unit reads as a unit, and the interface says so wherever it is shown.

elevation.note: Floor-to-floor elevations are not verified. Until they are, floors cannot be stacked at a real height and the container stays labelled a parametric reconstruction study.

slab.note: No verified overall plan, so no floor-wide slab extent.

grid.note: No accepted column or structural grid.

rooms.placementNote: Working layout, taken as the unit origin. The kitchen's plan region is anchored; its position within the unit is not.
Working layout. Neither the room boundary nor its position in the unit is anchored.
Working layout. Neither the room boundary nor its position in the unit is anchored.

_layers_note: Labels live in rooms/manifest.json now, so the rail has them whichever composition is loaded. The set of layers a build actually contains is discovered from its part specs rather than declared here.

viewModes.note: Camera mode and shell treatment are independent: the shell treatment applies in each of the three cameras, except cutaway, which means nothing in a plan because a plan is already a cut. The section plane and the exploded stack are display states over the same geometry — none of them creates, destroys, or re-parents anything, and the object count is identical with each of them on and off.

loading.note: A level outside the detail set never has its parts generated: it contributes one massing block per unit and nothing else. Focusing a scope on an unloaded level builds it and lets the level it replaced fall back to massing. Massing blocks are not components — no addresses, not indexed, not in the object count — and are reported separately.
loading.override: A full-detail switch builds every level at once. It exists so the cost and the saving can be compared rather than asserted.

composition.note: Room-to-room placement has no accepted anchor. The arrangement is a working layout, not an evidenced plan. Rooms 205 and 206 are unresolved volumes, so both their extents and their positions carry no claim.
